title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The title and outlet record indicate that a lawyer in Minnesota was suspended in connection with submitting fake case citations attributed to AI, a failure mode in which a generative AI system produces plausible-looking legal citations that do not correspond to real cases. This kind of error occurs at the point of use, when a practitioner relies on AI-generated output without independently verifying each citation against an authoritative legal database. A verification step, standard in legal research practice, would have caught fabricated references before they reached a court filing.

The failure here is a model asserting false information in the form of realistic but nonexistent case law, used outside the conditions of supervised legal research. The deployment context is a professional legal setting where accuracy of citation carries formal consequences, and no human check appears to have caught the output before submission.

What is not established from the available information is the specific AI system involved, the precise number or nature of the citations at issue, or any findings of intent on the lawyer's part, as the article text was not recoverable for review.
